etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin distinctus, perfect passive participle of distinguere (“to push apart, to divide”), + -ive (forming adjectives signifying relation or tendency to). Cognate with French distinctif and Medieval Latin distinctivus.

definitions.definition: Distinguishing, used to or enabling the distinguishing of some thing.

quote.citation: 1583, Philip Stubbes, The Anatomie of Abuses, Folio V:
quote.text: Our Apparell was giuen vs as a signe distinctiue to discern betwixt sex and sex.

definitions.definition: (rare) Discriminating, discerning, having the ability to distinguish between things.

quote.citation: 1650, Thomas Browne, chapter 3, in Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC, 2nd book, page 75:
1856, John Ruskin, Modern Painters […], volume III, London: Smith, Elder and Co., […], →OCLC, part IV (Of Many Things), page 293:
quote.text: Wordsworth's distinctive work was a war with pomp and pretence, and a display of the majesty of simple feelings and humble hearts.

definitions.definition: (rare) Distinguished, being distinct in character or position.

quote.citation: 1867, Samuel Smiles, chapter XVII, in The Huguenots, page 432:
quote.text: The refugees... at length ceased to exist as a distinctive body among the people.

definitions.definition: (Hebrew grammar, of accents) Used to separate clauses in place of stops.

quote.citation: 1874, Andrew Bruce Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar, page 27:
quote.text: These are the main distinctive accents, and by stopping at them... the reader will do justice to the sense.

definitions.definition: (linguistics, of sounds) Distinguishing a particular sense of word.

quote.citation: 1927, L. Bloomfield et al., Language, number 3, page 129:
quote.text: Normally we symbolize only phonemes (distinctive features) so far as we can determine them.

definitions.definition: A distinctive thing: a quality or property permitting distinguishing; a characteristic.

quote.citation: 1816, Maurice Keatinge, Travels through France and Spain to Morocco, volume I, page 189:
quote.text: ...the red umbrella, the distinctive of royalty here...

quote.citation: 1874, Andrew Bruce Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar, page 27:
quote.text: A distinctive of less power than Zakeph is Ṭiphḥâ.

definitions.definition: (theology) A distinctive belief, tenet, or dogma of a denomination or sect.

quote.citation: 1979, Theron F. Schlabach, “Gospel versus Gospel”, in Studies in Anabaptist and Mennonite History, page 154:
quote.text: Mennonites could go forth somewhat detached from the chauvinism of Western culture—but not so from the Mennonite distinctives.
